question.text: Vatsalya Charitable Society (child-welfare NPO) received INR 12 lakh of donations during the year where the donors' identities were NOT recorded. Total donations for the year were INR 2 crore. How will the SIA flag this for tax treatment in the pre-engagement note?

answer.text: The entire INR 12 lakh is fully exempt because the NPO is 12AB registered
Anonymous donations above the higher of INR 1 lakh or 5% of total donations are taxed at 30% under Section 115BBI
Anonymous donations are taxed at the marginal slab rate applicable to the donor
Anonymous donations up to 25% of total donations are exempt; balance taxed at 20%

explanation.text: The Logic: Anonymous donations received by a charitable NPO are taxed at a flat 30% under the Income Tax Act, but only to the extent they exceed a threshold of the HIGHER of INR 1 lakh or 5% of total donations for the year. Registration under Section 12AB does not shield anonymous donations, and the tax falls on the recipient NPO rather than on the donor. For Vatsalya Charitable Society with total donations of INR 2 crore, 5% = INR 10 lakh, which is higher than INR 1 lakh, so anonymous donations beyond INR 10 lakh are taxed at 30%. The Trap: Full exemption ignores the anti-abuse rule that overrides 12AB protection for anonymous receipts. Donor-side slab taxation is irrelevant because the charge is on the NPO. The "25% exempt / 20% balance" option is fabricated and does not exist in the statute. Note: The Social Impact Assessors workbook confirms that anonymous donations received by a charitable NPO are taxable at a flat 30%, but the cited pages do not explicitly set out the "higher of INR 1 lakh or 5% of total donations" threshold. That threshold framing is drawn from Section 115BBC of the Income Tax Act rather than from the workbook pages checked.
